newsitem.title: USA: Brokerage sued over hedge-to-arrive deals - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Brokerage sued over hedge-to-arrive deals - lawyer.

text.p: A lawyer said Wednesday he has filed a class-action lawsuit against Farmers Commodity Corp (FCC) to recoup losses stemming from so-called hedge-to-arrive grain contracts.
Officials of FCC, a commodity brokerage based in Des Moines, Iowa, were not immediately available for comment.

Attorney Bart McLeay of Omaha, Nebraska, said he filed a class-action lawsuit against FCC last Friday in U.S. District Court in Omaha. McLeay said he represented two farmers, C. Everret Wilkens and Robin Heyen, who entered into hedge-to-arrive contracts with FCC.
"We believe (FCC) is a responsible party for damages that have been incurred by these farmers and other farmers who would be similarly situated," McLeay said.
McLeay said he would not immediately comment on specifics of the case, but he did say the contracts involved corn and wheat. He said his clients were seeking an unspecified amount of damages.

"There's no specific amount listed in the complaint. We will make a determination of the specific amount of damages at the trial," McLeay said. "We have literally just filed the complaint. There hasn't been a response even by (FCC) or anyone acting in their behalf.

Hedge-to-arrive contracts involve grain sales in which the price or delivery date can be set at a later date. Some versions allow sales to be "rolled" to another month or year. In some cases, they have been blamed for creating financial stress when market prices move higher than expected.
